verdict.rationale: Bento's own 'signals' let users describe a failure mode in plain English. Bento then trains a detector on their traces, fires it in real time and backfills history, and each signal's prompt and config can be edited. That makes signals a configurable, natural-language evaluator over outputs, and releases are 'scored' offline, in CI and on live traffic. However, the docs never say these detectors are LLM-as-a-judge graders, and they describe no score scales, rubrics or judge-model choice. missing for 10: explicit LLM-as-a-judge mechanism, configurable judge model/rubric/score outputs, documentation of evaluator scoring results, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can score outputs with configurable LLM-as-a-judge evaluators
